tasks.original_prompt:
Latest hemoglobin still below normal for this patient? Then flag that report with a follow-up task; if not, don't touch the chart.
Context: patient MRN SYN-81380fcffe (identifier system https://fhir-workflows.example/mrn); as-of date 2021-10-21, treated as today.
Answer contract: reply with only a JSON object with exactly two keys, answer and evidence. Consider only Observations coded LOINC 718-7 (hemoglobin) with status final or corrected and an effective date on or before the as-of date, in date order. A result is low when its value is below 12.0 g/dL for a patient whose Patient.gender is female and below 13.0 g/dL otherwise. answer is {"latest": ..., "still_low": ..., "task_created": ...}. latest is the most recent result, with exactly these keys: date (string: effective date, YYYY-MM-DD), value (number: valueQuantity.value exactly as recorded) and unit (string: valueQuantity.unit); still_low (boolean) is whether it is low; both are null when no result was ever low. Only when still_low is true, create exactly this record (and nothing else), replacing $patient with the resolved Patient reference and $report with the DiagnosticReport whose basedOn references the ServiceRequest the latest result's basedOn references and whose result lists the latest result: {"resourceType": "Task", "status": "requested", "intent": "order", "for": {"reference": "$patient"}, "focus": {"reference": "$report"}}. task_created (boolean) is whether you created it. evidence lists the resolved Patient and every record used for the answer (the latest result, and its DiagnosticReport when you create the Task; when no result was ever low, every hemoglobin result considered), using retrieved Type/id references and nothing else. Change nothing else in the chart.
tasks.prompt:
SYN-81380fcffe: as of 2021-10-21, if the most recent hemoglobin is still low, add a follow-up task to that lab report; otherwise leave the chart unchanged.
Reply with only JSON: {"answer": {latest: {date: date YYYY-MM-DD, unit: text, value: number}, still_low: true/false, task_created: true/false}, "evidence": [references of the records you used, Type/id]}. Use null for any value the chart does not have.
tasks.prompt_before_v023: SYN-81380fcffe: as of 2021-10-21, if the most recent hemoglobin result is still low, add a follow-up task to that lab report; otherwise leave the chart unchanged.
required_changes: only if the patient's most recent hemoglobin is low, add a follow-up task for the patient on the lab report listing that result; otherwise change nothing
rewrite_changes: only if the patient's most recent hemoglobin is low, create a new Task (status requested, intent order) for the patient whose focus is the lab report (DiagnosticReport) listing that most recent result; otherwise change nothing

tasks.original_prompt:
ED follow-up audit for this patient: last emergency visit date, first clinic visit after it and the gap in days, whether it met 30 days, and the measurements from that clinic visit, plus the ED note.
Context: patient MRN SYN-81380fcffe (identifier system https://fhir-workflows.example/mrn); as-of date 2021-09-13, treated as today.
Answer contract: reply with only a JSON object with exactly two keys, answer and evidence. The ED visit is the most recent Encounter with class code EMER, status finished and a period start on or before the as-of date. The follow-up visit is the earliest Encounter with class code AMB and status finished whose period start date is after the ED visit's start date, at most 90 days after it, and on or before the as-of date; when there is none, followup_date and days_to_followup are null, within_30_days is false and measurements is empty. answer is {"ed_visit_date": ..., "followup_date": ..., "days_to_followup": ..., "within_30_days": ..., "measurements": [...]}. The dates are period start dates (YYYY-MM-DD); days_to_followup (integer) is the number of days between them; within_30_days (boolean) is days_to_followup <= 30. measurements has one entry for every Observation whose encounter references the follow-up Encounter and has a valueQuantity, and one for every component with a valueQuantity of such an Observation (a blood pressure panel gives systolic and diastolic), sorted by code, each with exactly these keys: code (string: the first code.coding code of the Observation or component), date (string: effective date, YYYY-MM-DD), value (number: valueQuantity.value exactly as recorded) and unit (string: valueQuantity.unit). evidence lists the resolved Patient and every record used for the answer (both Encounters, the DocumentReference whose context references the ED Encounter, and each listed Observation), using retrieved Type/id references and nothing else. This is read-only: do not change the chart.
tasks.prompt:
For MRN SYN-81380fcffe, as of 2021-09-13, pull the most recent ED visit date, the first ambulatory clinic visit after that (within 90 days), calculate the days between, note if it was within 30 days, list all measurements from that clinic visit, and include the ED note.
Reply with only JSON: {"answer": {days_to_followup: number, ed_visit_date: date YYYY-MM-DD, followup_date: date YYYY-MM-DD, measurements: list of {code: text, date: date YYYY-MM-DD, unit: text, value: number}, within_30_days: true/false}, "evidence": [references of the records you used, Type/id]}. Use null for any value the chart does not have.

Return review_requested=true and prescription_changed=false.
